subject: Literacy
title: Who, what and where?
objectives: Children will answer simple who, what and where questions.
Children will ask a simple question such as "What is that?"
content: Answering who, what and where questions and asking a simple question such as "What is that?"
teachingActivities: Ask one question at a time and wait at least five seconds; use real objects and people; accept a word, a point or a gesture; model the question "What is that?" often.
learnerActivities: Answer who, what and where questions with a word or phrase and ask one simple question.
resources: A hiding place such as a box or a cloth
assessment: Observe whether each child answers who, what and where questions and asks at least one question.
expectedOutcomes: Answers who, what and where questions with a word or phrase.
crossCurricular: Understanding the World: people and places

lessons.title: Who is it?
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will answer the question "Who is it?" about a person or a toy.
successCriteria: Points to or names a person when asked who
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name people, objects and animals and use short phrases to ask for things.
lessons.starter: Hold up a photograph of the teacher and ask "Who is it?" Say "It is Teacher."
teacherActivities: Show a photograph and ask "Who is it?" and answer yourself the first time.
Show a second photograph and wait for the child to answer.
Ask "Who is that?" about a friend in the circle.
Let children ask "Who is it?" about a photograph.
learnerActivities: Child says the name or points.
Child names or points to the friend.
Child asks and the group answers.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show a photograph and ask "Who is it?" and answer yourself the first time. Children: Children look and listen.
Step 2. Teacher: Show a second photograph and wait for the child to answer. Children: Child says the name or points.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask "Who is that?" about a friend in the circle. Children: Child names or points to the friend.
Step 4. Teacher: Let children ask "Who is it?" about a photograph. Children: Child asks and the group answers.

practical.title: Who is it?
steps: Ask "Who is it?" and let children answer.
Let each child hold a photograph and ask a friend.
practical.safety: Handle photographs gently and return them. Be sensitive and do not use photographs of children whose families have not agreed.

differentiation.support: Offer two photographs and say the answer with the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find a friend and ask "Who is it?"

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Who is it?
questions.expected: The name of the person in the photograph.

expectedOutcomes: Answers who questions with a word or point
lessons.conclusion: Put the photographs away and say goodbye to each person.
lessons.homeConnection: Look at family photographs and ask "Who is it?" for each person.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "answer the question "Who is it?" about a person or a toy" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: What is it?
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will answer "What is it?" and ask "What is that?"
successCriteria: Names an object when asked what
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name people, objects and animals and use short phrases to ask for things.
resources: A mystery box with a ball, a cup, a spoon and a toy car
lessons.starter: Shake the mystery box and say "What is in the box? What is it?"
teacherActivities: Take out one object and ask "What is it?" Wait for the answer.
Show the child how to ask "What is that?" by pointing to the box.
Cover an object with the cloth and ask "What is it?"
Let each child take an object from the box and ask the group.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Take out one object and ask "What is it?" Wait for the answer. Children: Child names the object.
Step 2. Teacher: Show the child how to ask "What is that?" by pointing to the box. Children: Child asks or points.
Step 3. Teacher: Cover an object with the cloth and ask "What is it?" Children: Child guesses or names it.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child take an object from the box and ask the group. Children: Child asks "What is it?"

practical.title: Mystery box
steps: Put four objects in a box.
Each child takes one out and says what it is.
practical.safety: Use large safe objects only. Keep the objects clean and supervise handling.

differentiation.support: Offer two objects and say the word with the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to put an object in the box and ask a friend to guess.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What is that?
questions.expected: The name of what is pointed to.

lessons.conclusion: Put all objects back in the box and say "Goodbye."
lessons.homeConnection: Ask your child "What is that?" when you walk together and wait for an answer.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "answer "What is it?" and ask "What is that?"" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Where is it?
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will answer "Where is it?" by pointing or using a word such as in or on.
successCriteria: Points to where an object is
Says in, on or here with support
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name people, objects and animals and use short phrases to ask for things.
lessons.starter: Hide the teddy bear in the box and ask "Where is teddy? Where is he?"
teacherActivities: Ask "Where is teddy?" and wait for children to look and point.
Say "Teddy is in the box" and show the word in.
Put teddy on the chair and ask "Where is teddy now?"
Let each child hide teddy and ask "Where is teddy?"
learnerActivities: Children look and point to the box.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Ask "Where is teddy?" and wait for children to look and point. Children: Children look and point to the box.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "Teddy is in the box" and show the word in. Children: Children say "in".
Step 3. Teacher: Put teddy on the chair and ask "Where is teddy now?" Children: Child points or says "on".
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child hide teddy and ask "Where is teddy?" Children: Child hides and friends answer.

practical.title: Hide teddy
steps: Children look and point to where he is.
practical.safety: Hide teddy in easy places away from hazards. Keep children together and supervise looking.

differentiation.support: Point and say "teddy is in the box" with the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to hide teddy and tell where he is.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Where is teddy?
questions.expected: In the box or on the chair.

expectedOutcomes: Uses in or on with support
lessons.conclusion: Put teddy to bed and say goodnight.
lessons.homeConnection: Hide a toy at home and ask "Where is it?"
teacherReflection: Which children could show "answer "Where is it?" by pointing or using a word such as in or on" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Who, what, where game
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will answer who, what and where questions in a game.
successCriteria: Answers a who, what or where question
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name people, objects and animals and use short phrases to ask for things.
resources: Three question cards: who, what, where
lessons.starter: Show the three question cards and say "Who? What? Where?" Ask the children to repeat.
teacherActivities: Pick a card and ask the matching question with a photograph or toy.
Pick another card and ask again.
Let a child pick a card and ask a friend.
learnerActivities: Children answer with a word or gesture.
Child asks and the friend answers.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Pick a card and ask the matching question with a photograph or toy. Children: Children answer with a word or gesture.
Step 2. Teacher: Pick another card and ask again. Children: Children answer.
Step 3. Teacher: Let a child pick a card and ask a friend. Children: Child asks and the friend answers.
Step 4. Teacher: Play the game in pairs. Children: Children ask and answer.

practical.title: Question game
steps: Put three cards in a basket.
A child picks a card and asks the question.
The friend answers with a point or word.
practical.safety: Supervise pairs and keep voices gentle. Help children who are shy by accepting gestures.

differentiation.support: Ask the question with the child and give a picture clue.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to ask a friend two different questions.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Answers who, what and where questions
lessons.conclusion: Put the cards back and say goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Ask your child who, what and where questions at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "answer who, what and where questions in a game" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 8 questions check
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child answers and asks questions.
successCriteria: Answers who, what and where questions
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name people, objects and animals and use short phrases to ask for things.
lessons.starter: Say "Who? What? Where?" and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: who, what and where.
At each station ask the matching question and wait.
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Child answers with a word or gesture.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: who, what and where. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask the matching question and wait. Children: Child answers with a word or gesture.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Question stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep floors clear. Use only safe objects.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use real objects.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to ask a friend a question.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: answers who questions; answers what questions; answers where questions; asks one question.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 8
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye to teddy and the box.
lessons.homeConnection: Ask questions at home and wait for your child to answer.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child answers and asks questions" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
